cards.q: Stateful vs stateless: Security Group or NACL?
cards.a: Security Group = stateful (return traffic auto-allowed), instance level. NACL = stateless (must allow return traffic both ways), subnet level, numbered rules evaluated ascending.

cards.q: S3 SSE-S3 vs SSE-KMS vs SSE-C — who holds the key?
cards.a: SSE-S3: AWS-managed keys, no KMS audit. SSE-KMS: KMS key w/ key policy + CloudTrail audit, per-request cost. SSE-C: you supply key per request over HTTPS, AWS stores nothing.
AssumeRole: existing identity or cross-account assumes role, temp creds. AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity: federate external OIDC IdP (Cognito, Google) without AWS credentials.

cards.q: Secrets Manager vs SSM Parameter Store?
cards.a: Secrets Manager: native auto-rotation (RDS etc.), higher $/secret, cross-region replication. Parameter Store: cheaper, SecureString w/ KMS, rotation needs custom logic.

cards.q: ALB vs NLB — pick for which cases?
cards.a: ALB: L7 HTTP/S/gRPC, path/host routing, WAF, sticky sessions. NLB: L4 TCP/TLS/UDP, extreme perf, static/Elastic IP, preserves client IP, no WAF.

cards.q: SQS vs SNS vs EventBridge — one line each?
cards.a: SQS: point-to-point queue, pull, decoupling/buffer. SNS: pub/sub fan-out push. EventBridge: event bus w/ rule filtering, SaaS+AWS sources, many targets.

cards.q: RDS Multi-AZ vs Read Replicas — availability or performance?
cards.a: Multi-AZ: sync standby other AZ, HA failover only, standby not readable. Read Replicas: async, scale reads, promotable, cross-region for DR.
Backup & Restore -> Pilot Light (core replicated, minimal running) -> Warm Standby (scaled-down full copy) -> Multi-Site Active/Active (full scale both regions).

cards.q: ASG target tracking vs step vs scheduled scaling?
cards.a: Target tracking: keep metric at target, simplest, preferred. Step: scale in bands around alarm. Scheduled: known predictable load patterns.

cards.q: EBS gp3 vs gp2 — the upgrade math?
cards.a: gp3: 3000 IOPS + 125 MB/s baseline free, provision to 16k IOPS/1000 MB/s, 20% cheaper. gp2: IOPS tied to size (3 IOPS/GB) + burst buckets.
15 min max run, 10,240 MB memory, 1000 default concurrency, /tmp 10,240 MB, zip 50MB compressed, container image 10GB.

cards.q: DynamoDB on-demand vs provisioned — when each?
cards.a: On-demand: unpredictable/spiky/unknown load, pay per request. Provisioned + auto scaling: predictable load, cheaper at scale; reserved capacity for very steady.
CloudFront: L7 HTTP(S) edge caching, signed URLs, OAC. Global Accelerator: any TCP/UDP, no caching, static anycast IPs, healthy regional routing over AWS backbone.

cards.q: Aurora read replica limits vs RDS?
cards.a: Aurora: up to 15 replicas, shared storage (lag ~0), fast promotion. RDS: 5 replicas (MySQL/MariaDB/Postgres), async, lag possible.
Std-IA min 30d, Glacier Instant Retrieval min 90d, Deep Archive min 180d. Early transition still bills the full minimum.

cards.q: Spot instances — right vs wrong workloads?
cards.a: Right: stateless, fault-tolerant, batch, distributed, ASG mixed instances. Wrong: stateful DBs, SPOFs, can't survive 2-min interruption notice.
Savings Plans: commit $/hr, flexible across family/size/OS/region. RIs: commit to instance attributes + capacity reservation option. Both 1-3yr, ~30-72% off.

cards.q: When is Aurora Serverless v2 the exam answer?
cards.a: Unpredictable/infrequent DB load, dev/test, multi-tenant SaaS, no capacity planning — fine-grained scaling (vs v1's on/off ACUs).
